text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed higher across the board, boosted by speculative buying and a technical breakthrough by New York futures. May ended up $25 at $1,578 per tonne and July rose $30 to $1,592. July resistance was pegged at a gap between $1,611 and $1,620 while support was seen at $1,546. Arabica futures in New York erased sharp early gains to finish mainly lower on Tuesday, as speculators led a late sell-off in anticipation of a build-up in U.S. stockpiles, dealers said.

Spot May delivery fell 3.60 cents/lb on the day to 192.40 cents, after trading from 201.50 to 191.00. Second month July settled 2.35 cents lower at 174.65 while the back months closed up 2.50 to down 2.60. The May/July switch narrowed to 17.75 cents/lb, against 19.00 cents at the close on Friday.

After the close, the Green Coffee Association released its stock figures and the increase was a mere 111,000 bags, far below earlier expectations of 250,000 to 700,000 bags. The lower than expected outcome could prove to be extremely bullish for Wednesday's session. Technically, traders pegged May support at 190 cents, then 187 cents. May's next upside objective was seen at 205 cents with some seeing 225 as a reasonable upside target.

UNITED KINGDOM - Certified coffee stocks held in LIFFE (London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange) nominated warehouses totalled 4,008 5-tonne lots at the end of March, a LIFFE statement said. This compares to 2,801 lots in February and 2,831 in January.

BRAZIL - Brazilian stevedores will go on national strike in sympathy with their colleagues at Santos at midnight Thursday (0300 GMT Friday) for 48 hours, a union official said. Stevedores at Santos began an indefinite strike at 0700 local in protest against steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) using its own workers to load and unload vessels at its private terminal at the port. The national strike represented the second nationwide stoppage in two weeks.

UNITED STATES - Supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses rose in March by 111,000 60-kg bags, to 1.657 million bags, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported. Most analysts had forecast an increase of between 250,000 and 700,000 bags after Latin America shipped heavily over the last several weeks to take advantage of higher futures prices.

It is now believed that the smaller than expected increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks will result in a boost for New York coffee futures. Port of New Orleans posted the largest gain in coffee stocks rising by 74,000 bags to 551,000, the GCA said. Inventories increased by 37,000 bags to 319,000 in Laredo, Texas, a major receiving point for Mexican coffee while warehouse stocks in San Francisco rose 24,000 bags to 141,000 bags. Stocks in Houston decreased by 36,000 bags to 158,000 bags.

COLOMBIA - Colombian private coffee exporters have over- registered exports for the April/June period by 116,000 60-kg bags and the National Coffee Federation is threatening not to honor the sales which exceed the allocated export quota for the period. Private exporters are hoping to find a solution in negotiations with Jorge Cardenas, the Coffee Federation president. Some exporters thought the allocated quota agreement was not working thus explaining the over- registration.

BELGIUM-LUXEMBOURG - Coffee imports in October 1996 amounted to 166,132 bags, down from 203,473 imported in October 1995. This brought cumulative imports in January/October 1996 to 1.900 million bags, roughly 11 percent up on the tonnage imported in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 reached 2.068 million bags compared to 2.234 million in 1994.

Major suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Brazil (210,200 vs 189,300 bags), Uganda (137,800 vs 39,900 bags), France (142,100 vs 150,600 bags) and Kenya (122,500 vs 17,800). Coffee exports in October 1996 amounted to 76,986 bags compared to 113,929 in October 1995. This brought cumulative exports in January/October 1996 to 716,007 bags, almost 25 percent down on the volume exported in January/October 1995. Total exports in 1995 reached 1.204 million bags compared with 1.294 million in 1994. Belgium ships most of its coffee roast and ground with France (143,300 vs 470,600 bags) and the Netherlands (102,800 vs 49,700 bags) the main markets.
